subject: Standard errors (and confidence intervals) for indirect effect in the std.all solution

messages.author: 9633d779a02b841e
messages.subject: Standard errors (and confidence intervals) for indirect effect in the std.all solution
parts:
Hi everybody,

I'm trying to get the standard errors and confidence intervals for the standardized (std.all) indirect effects of my mediation model.
I can only obtain the estimate but I cannot figure out a way to obtain se and ci (like for exemple in Mplus when OUTPUT: SDTYX is used)

If I use:
standardizedSolution(fit)
it only gives my standardized estimate but NA for the standard errors.

I would like to obtain bootstrapped ci, but this seems difficult since I'm using MLR estimator.
If I try to get bootstrap ci using bootstrapLavaan(fit), the output doest not include the defined parameters.

PS. Using std.lv=TRUE in sem() function changes the metric of the model and leads to slightly different estimates, so I would like to avoid that.

Any advice would be appreciated!

Thanks

massimiliano

messages.subject: Re: Standard errors (and confidence intervals) for indirect effect in the std.all solution
parts:
I'm trying to get the standard errors and confidence intervals for the standardized (std.all) indirect effects of my mediation model.
I can only obtain the estimate but I cannot figure out a way to obtain se and ci (like for exemple in Mplus when OUTPUT: SDTYX is used)

The usual recommendation is to test null hypotheses about the raw parameters, and just interpret standardized estimates as standardized measures of effect size.  The adjustments to SEs of standardized estimates should lead to the same inferences as the raw parameters' SEs.
I would like to obtain bootstrapped ci, but this seems difficult since I'm using MLR estimator.

If you want bootstrapped CIs to test null hypotheses, you don't need to adjust the SEs or chi-squared using MLR.  The point estimates in MLR are not adjusted, they are the same as ML estimates.  So you can just use bootstrapped CIs to test parameters and the Bollen-Stine bootstrap for chi-squared.
If I try to get bootstrap ci using bootstrapLavaan(fit), the output doest not include the defined parameters.

bootstrapLavaan() accepts any function you give it.  So you can just define a function the returns the user-defined parameters from the appropriate rows/column of the standardizedSolution() output, then submit that function to bootstrapLavaan().  See an example in the Details section of the ?bootstrapLavaan help page.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
